raw_content:
Here is a Semgrep rule that matches the vulnerable behavior and avoids matching the patched behavior:

```yaml
---
id: vuln-felix-dev-87513ea3
title: "Potential XSS in Apache Felix Web Console"
description: "Apache Felix Web Console is prone to Cross Site Scripting (XSS) attacks due to lack of proper encoding."
severity: WARNING
language: java

patterns:
  - name: xss-vulnerability
    signature: >
      Matcher.anyOf(
        Matcher.method("jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest", "getParameter").withArgs("filter"),
        Matcher.field("org.apache.felix.webconsole.internal.core.ServicesServlet", "FILTER_PARAM")
      ).hasNext(Matcher.anyOf(
        Matcher.method("org.owasp.encoder.Encode", "forHtmlContent").withArgs(Matcher.any()),
        Matcher.method("org.apache.felix.webconsole.internal.util.Util", "encodeForHTML").withArgs(Matcher.any())
      ))
    taint-mode: WRITE
```

This rule will match if the `filter` parameter in a request to the Apache Felix Web Console is not properly encoded before being used in an HTML context, which can lead to XSS attacks. The `taint-mode` field specifies that this pattern should be applied on writes (i.e., when data is outputted).

Please note that this rule might need adjustments depending on the exact version of Apache Felix Web Console you are using and how it handles encoding.
